newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives to promise more tax breaks - BBC.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives to promise more tax breaks - BBC.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative party will offer a tax break for couples where one partner gives up work to take care of children or sick relatives, BBC radio reported on Wednesday.

It said the promise would formally be unveiled when the party released its manifesto at 0830 GMT on Wednesday. The Conservatives are trailing the opposition Labour party by a large margin ahead of the May 1 election.

The BBC said the tax break -- which would also apply to those who stayed at home to take care of elderly relatives -- could be worth as much as 20 stg a week to couples where one partner was earning the average national wage.
The Daily Mail newspaper said the measure would cost more than one billion stg a year. Around two million people would be eligible.
The BBC said the Conservatives would also pledge to reduce the basic income tax rate to 20 percent from the current 23 percent. The party has consistently promised to gradually cut the basic rate.
